The purpose-built Tesla Cybercab is expanding to more U.S. cities after its launch in Austin.

After 135,000 miles, Edmunds’ cheap used Model S still has useful range and enough performance to make it look tempting.

Edmunds bought one to see how much car you actually get for the money, and its first round of testing makes a pretty good case for taking the gamble. Its Model S has covered 135,000 miles, yet it still managed 221 miles in the Edmunds EV range test. That’s not great compared to a new electric sedan, but it’s still very good given the price.

It’s still pretty quick, too. In the video documenting its first series of tests, the single-motor, rear-wheel-drive Tesla hits 60 mph in five seconds and completes the quarter-mile in 13.3 seconds. That’s on old, mismatched tires that struggle to put down all the power.

Edmunds quotes an original MSRP of $69,900, which matches the base Model S 60. But its five-second sprint to 60 mph and 221-mile range suggest the price may be misleading; this is likely the larger-battery Model S 85, which started at $79,900. Its design has its roots nearly two decades ago, when Tesla began developing the Model S in 2007. It showed the first design concept two years later, and the final production version, which began production in 2012, stayed remarkably true to the look of the 2009 study.
